question: Can a testable click-to-move build be assembled from what is currently recovered?
answer: Not yet, and the remaining gap is engine startup rather than any single missing function.

what_is_recovered.movement: recovered contracts drive a click request, path search and bounded frames with monotonic progress toward the target; verified by a frozen receipt (2 frames / 300 assertions) and by a live observation on the original client
what_is_recovered.window: the shipped WinWindow constructor and Initialize execute in our own process and produced a real HWND
what_is_recovered.engine_object: GraphicsEngine and GraphicsEngineSettings construct correctly with relocated vtables; the settings default to the direct3d11 plugin name
what_is_recovered.present_contract: PresentSurface issues IDXGISwapChain::Present through vtable slot 0x40 under the object lock
what_is_recovered.renderer_module: Direct3D11.dll identified, 164 exports enumerated, RenderDevice vtable (40 slots) and the device constructor decoded

the_blocker.fact: Engine.dll+0x421428 is null in a process that merely loads the module, and CreateDevice dereferences it unconditionally.
the_blocker.searches: no direct store to it exists in Engine.dll or Game.dll, no LEA takes its address, and it is absent from the relocation table
the_blocker.static_neighbourhood: the surrounding slots are a table of pointer-like values, and neighbouring singletons are published by lazy-create helpers and cleared by a shutdown path at 0x76a9d
the_blocker.interpretation: the global is published by engine startup code that has not been located, not by a simple assignment we can mirror

why_it_matters: Standing up the real engine startup would be re-implementing the game bootstrap. Substituting a hand-made engine object would violate the requirement that presentation come from the reverse-engineered code.

options.a: keep recovering the engine startup path: locate _initterm initialisers and the publisher of 0x421428 (static, offline, no approval needed)
options.b: scope the first testable build to movement plus the recovered window, with presentation explicitly marked as not yet recovered
options.c: use the original Game.dll startup as the host (running the shipped client) and instrument only the recovered contracts

recommendation: Option a is the honest continuation and needs no approval; option b would not satisfy the stated requirement that presentation be recovered; option c crosses into hosting the original binary, which needs an explicit decision.
not_claimed: that a device can be created
that a frame can be presented
that a testable click-to-move build exists
